info.title: NOX Energy API - Battery
info.description:
# Battery API Documentation

This documentation shows only the endpoints available to battery users.

**Preview:** these endpoints are documented ahead of their release and currently answer
`501 Not Implemented`.

## Authentication

1. Get your API key from [NOX Energy](mailto:support@nox.energy).
2. Include the API key in your API calls with the header: `x-api-key: YOUR_API_KEY`.

## Access Level

This documentation is specifically for **battery users** who have access to these endpoints.

Base URL: [https://api.nox.energy](https://api.nox.energy)

get.description:
**Preview: not available yet.** This endpoint is documented ahead of its release and currently
answers `501 Not Implemented`. Its contract may still change before release.

Get information about all NOX-connected batteries associated with your energy supplier account.


 * `allowed_modes` lists the battery modes the battery accepts in a schedule. They depend on the
battery model and on the other devices in its household.

 * `min_soc_pct` is the lower limit for `force_discharge`: below it, NOX Energy takes control and
puts the battery in the default mode `auto`. It does not limit `auto` itself, where the battery may
keep covering the house load. It is fixed at 20 % for now.

 * `max_soc_pct` is the upper limit for `force_charge`: above it, NOX Energy takes control and
puts the battery in the default mode `auto`. It does not limit `auto` itself, where pv surplus may
keep charging the battery. It is fixed at 80 % for now.

 * The optimization settings of a battery are available with `GET /v1/devices/battery/settings`.

The battery modes:


 * `auto` (default): the battery follows its own logic. Pv surplus charges the battery, the battery
covers the house load, the grid covers the rest. The battery returns to `auto` outside your
schedules and whenever NOX Energy takes over.

 * `pause_charge`: the battery does not charge. Pv surplus is exported, the battery can still
discharge.

 * `pause_discharge`: the battery does not discharge. The grid covers the house load, pv surplus
can still charge the battery.

 * `force_charge`: the battery charges at its fixed charge power, from pv first and from the grid
for the rest. Only while the state of charge is below `max_soc_pct`: when it reaches that limit,
NOX Energy takes control and puts the battery in `auto` for the rest of the entry.

 * `force_discharge`: the battery discharges at its fixed discharge power, to the house first and
to the grid for the rest. Only while the state of charge is above `min_soc_pct`: when it reaches
that limit, NOX Energy takes control and puts the battery in `auto` for the rest of the entry.

If you want to know the response structure or possible enum values, like steerable reasons,
you can check it in the response model `schema`.

get.summary: Get Devices Battery Typical Charge Discharge Historical
get.description:
**Preview: not available yet.** This endpoint is documented ahead of its release and currently
answers `501 Not Implemented`. Its contract may still change before release.

Get the typical charge and discharge of your batteries in kWh for a specific timeframe with
15 min granularity.

This is a simulated baseline: how the battery would have behaved in `auto` (pure self-consumption),
using the realised pv production and house load. Compare it with the measured charge and discharge
to calculate the value of steering.

The timestamp refers to the 15 minutes after it. `soc_pct` is the state of charge at the end of
that interval.

The timestamp refers to the 15 minutes after it. `soc_pct` is the planned state of charge at the
end of that interval.

post.description:
**Preview: not available yet.** This endpoint is documented ahead of its release and currently
answers `501 Not Implemented`. Its contract may still change before release.

Submit battery schedules: per battery, a list of time windows with the battery mode to apply.
Schedules are only accepted for batteries with `flex_trading` enabled in their settings
(see `PATCH /v1/devices/battery/settings`).

`mode` can be set to:


 * `auto` (default): the battery follows its own logic. Pv surplus charges the battery, the battery
covers the house load, the grid covers the rest. The battery returns to `auto` outside your
schedules and whenever NOX Energy takes over.

 * `pause_charge`: the battery does not charge. Pv surplus is exported, the battery can still
discharge.

 * `pause_discharge`: the battery does not discharge. The grid covers the house load, pv surplus
can still charge the battery.

 * `force_charge`: the battery charges at its fixed charge power, from pv first and from the grid
for the rest. Only while the state of charge is below `max_soc_pct`: when it reaches that limit,
NOX Energy takes control and puts the battery in `auto` for the rest of the entry.

 * `force_discharge`: the battery discharges at its fixed discharge power, to the house first and
to the grid for the rest. Only while the state of charge is above `min_soc_pct`: when it reaches
that limit, NOX Energy takes control and puts the battery in `auto` for the rest of the entry.

Only the modes in the battery's `allowed_modes` are accepted. Outside your time windows the battery
falls back to `auto`. A `force_discharge` entry that starts while the state of charge is already at
or below `min_soc_pct`, or a `force_charge` entry that starts while it is already at or above
`max_soc_pct`, is accepted, but the battery stays in `auto` until the entry ends.

When you send a new schedule for a battery, it replaces every schedule previously sent for that
battery. You can send schedules for many batteries in one request.



 Timestamp fields in UTC. 

 Time format examples: 
 * 2023-10-01T00:00:00Z
 
 * 2023-10-01T00:00:00 


**NOTE**: 
 * The battery might need some time to react. `start_time` must be at least 1 minute in
the future.

patch.description:
**Preview: not available yet.** This endpoint is documented ahead of its release and currently
answers `501 Not Implemented`. Its contract may still change before release.

Update the settings of a single battery, or of all batteries of a user. To update a single battery,
only the `device_id` needs to be provided. To update all batteries of a user, provide the
`user_id` instead. Omitted settings are left unchanged.


 You can change the following settings:

 * Enable/Disable steering optimizations. `flex_trading` is mutually exclusive with the other
optimizations. The other optimizations can be enabled together.
 If `flex_trading` is enabled, we disable all other optimizations.
 If any other optimization is enabled, we disable `flex_trading`.
 If all optimizations are disabled, NOX Energy leaves the battery untouched.
 `flex_trading` means that you steer the battery with the schedules you provide to NOX Energy
 (see `POST /v1/devices/battery/schedules`).
 If you are a supplier that has a nox control package integration with Nox Energy, you should not
 enable `flex_trading` but instead the other optimization options like:
 `imbalance_optimization` to optimize the battery to minimize imbalances based on the imbalance prices of the users country.
 `dynamic_tariff` means that we will optimize the battery based on the day-ahead market prices of the users country.
 `pv_self_consumption` to optimize the battery to maximize self-consumption of pv production.
